question: In Figure 1B-1, what happens immediately after FHWA approves a request to experiment?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Figure 1B-1, once FHWA approves the request ("Approved?" → Yes), the next step is that the requesting jurisdiction installs the experimental traffic control device. From there, the process branches into evaluating the experimental device and providing semi-annual reports to the FHWA Division & HQ, ultimately concluding with the jurisdiction providing FHWA a copy of the final report. Standards (mandatory): - "A traffic control device or application that does not comply with the provisions of this Manual shall not be used on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel (see definition in Section 1C.02) without first receiving official approval to experiment from the FHWA's Office of Transportation Operations." (This is why installation occurs only after approval in the flowchart.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Figure 1B-1, where the "Yes" branch from the "Approved?" decision diamond leads directly to the box "Requesting jurisdiction installs experimental traffic control device," which then branches to "Evaluate experimental traffic control device" and "Requesting jurisdiction provides semi-annual reports to FHWA Division & HQ," both converging on "Requesting jurisdiction provides FHWA a copy of final report." [Image 5] shows the same Figure 1B-1 flowchart in the full-page context, confirming the sequence following approval. Citations: - Figure 1B-1 (p.7) - Section 1B.05 Support §9 (p.8) - Section 1B.05 Standard §2 (p.6) - Page 48
gold_answer: The requesting jurisdiction installs the experimental traffic control device.
